subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call — next steps / scheduling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: devops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call — next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the technical deep dive: 

- Recap from discovery:
  • Primary use: conversational triage + summarization for patient intake forms
  • Expected steady-state throughput: ~150–250 requests/sec (see note below)
  • Latency target: p95 < 200ms for inference responses
  • Model types: chat-based LLMs (context length ~2–4k tokens), occasional embeddings for similarity search

- What we need from the sizing call:
  1) Validate throughput and p95 latency targets with your traffic profile
  2) Confirm peak/seasonal factors and acceptable degradation/fallback policy
  3) Agree on autoscaling/burst strategy and SLA expectations for dedicated pools

I’ve attached a short capacity-template.xlsx to help capture traffic shape and peak windows. Please fill out the example rows and attach any sample request traces (if available) ahead of the call. I’ve also attached our Redwood Dedicated pricing summary for budgeting.

Availability: I can run a technical deep dive / sizing session next week. Two options we commonly use are:
  • Wed 23 Jun, 10:00 AM PT (recommended — includes our infra lead)
  • Thu 24 Jun, 3:00 PM PT

If neither works, send a couple of times that do and I’ll route a calendar invite. Attendees we suggest from your side: ML infra, SRE/DevOps, and an app owner. From our side I’ll bring Camila (technical lead) and Vivek (solutions architect).

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood-marissa/60min

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call — next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the high-level numbers from our end before we lock a time:

- Typical traffic: ~200 requests/sec average, with daily peaks ~380 req/sec (short bursts)
- Latency requirement: p95 <= 200ms, p99 ideally < 350ms
- Traffic model: mostly chat sessions, ~3k token context on average, spikes when batch intake processes run

We do have an internal requirement to ensure graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model/streaming) during sustained spikes. Also curious if Redwood supports configurable burst pools (we may want a 2x burst capacity for enrollment windows).

Both proposed times look doable. Wed 23 Jun 10:00 AM PT works for our SRE and ML infra. I’ll attach a short snapshot of recent traffic patterns (acme-traffic-snapshot.json) to help Camila prepare.

Thanks — Alex

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call — Wed 23 Jun 10:00 AM PT (tech lead + runbook)

Thanks for sending the traffic snapshot, Alex — I downloaded acme-traffic-snapshot.json and will use it to run a preliminary capacity estimate before Wednesday. A few quick notes and requests so we use the time efficiently: 

- Could you confirm the split between interactive requests and batch (e.g., 80/20)? That changes batching strategy recommendations.
- For the p95 < 200ms target: is that end-to-end (app + network + inference) or specifically inference-only? We size the Dedicated pool based on inference-only p95 and then add buffer for network/app overhead.
- Any constraints on test credentials or access to a staging endpoint for a short throughput run? If not, we can do an offline estimate from the snapshot.

I’ll bring a sizing runbook and our recommended autoscale config (burst pool + cooldown windows). Vivek will join to discuss model quantization options that may lower GPU footprint without compromising latency.

See you Wednesday — attaching a short pre-read (capacity-template.xlsx) that mirrors what we’ll walk through.

— Camila
Technical Lead, Dedicated Deployments | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: capacity-template.xlsx
